endonym.gloss: the cord that holds the walls

description.value: A three-metre length of twisted ribbon fibre carrying ninety-one knots in four sizes, recovered from the outer face of the midden bank where it had been thrown. Cords are rolled flat on the thigh from retted sweep ribbon and a knot is added or shifted at every handover, so a cord in working use is never in a finished state. This one had been retired, which is the only reason it is in the collection at all. The fibre is sound and the plait is tight; the salt has taken the colour off the shell markers, so the reading of the last twenty knots is irrecoverable.

notes.value: All four cords in the collection were thrown away before they were collected. No cord in use has ever been drawn or photographed, and the accession file notes, twice, that this is a condition of holding the four.
